<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **3** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## L1 review (L1-d) · 2026-11-17T16:58Z

L1: REWORK
Head-sha: `3c8835f8cf74ea69652b8af1c86f53bae3e39ecd`

Read against claim 6951290353 and report 6954290964 on #34706. Merge base `fc5913e1`, 24 files, +386/-37.
- **Not governed:** `check-governed-merges --branch` reports 0 paths and 423 lines.
- **CI at this head:** 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed.

This is **paper only**. Once the claim is amended, this head is ACCEPT with no push.

### What holds
- **Closing keyword.** `Fixes #34706` is right; all three items and their pins are done.
  1. **The inbox action.** Both `type: 'api'` handlers add one code-keyed rule to their existing refusal step: `useConsoleActionRuntime`'s `apiHandler`, and `RecordDetailView`'s door and direct legs through one `refused()` helper. On `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED_BEFORE_ACCEPTING_OR_REJECTING_INVITATION`, they navigate to `/verify-email-prompt?email=…&redirect=/accept-invitation/<id>` and answer `{ success: false }` with no toast. Every other refusal still goes through `apiActionRefusalResult`, and a CONTROL case pins that.
     - `accept_invitation`'s `ai.description` states main's condition. That text is agent-facing only and no generated bundle carries it.
     - No metadata key, spec change or server change was needed, so the claim's stop condition did not fire.
  2. **The verify page's copy.** Only `RegisterPage` sets `?sent=1`, and the dev measured that only the sign-up has sent a mail by then. Every other arrival asks the person to send. "Sent to:" and the spam hint appear only after `sentOnArrival || resent`.
     - The existing hand-off pins now pass `&sent=1` where the sign-up arrival is meant. That is the stated behaviour change, not a weakening.
     - The two new keys exist in all 11 locales.
  3. **Hosts.** The app-shell README ("Hosting the invitation pages") and the changeset name the route and its `email` / `redirect` keys.
- **Changeset.** It names all four packages whose `src/**` moved (`platform-objects`, `app-shell`, `console`, `i18n`, all patch). Its sentences match the diff. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` match the claim.
- **Tests.** Real commands with counts. Four ablations, each red and restored to HEAD: the hook routing, the `RecordDetailView` routing, `sentOnArrival`, and the register `sent=1`.
- **Scope.** `AcceptInvitationPage.tsx` is left as main has it (an overlap with draft #34883). The claim allows that, since it may narrow.

### Must-fix
- **M1 (paper): the claim surface needs an amendment.** The claim names the action file, "the console's api-action refusal path", `VerifyEmailPromptPage.tsx` and its locale strings, the item 3 docs, and *card-named* tests. These paths are outside it:
  - `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/RegisterPage.tsx` (the `sent=1` mark);
  - `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/verifyEmailPromptQuery.ts` (new);
  - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/orgErrorMessage.ts`. The claim said to *reuse* `isAcceptNeedsVerifiedEmail` from it; the PR adds `verifyEmailPromptPath` and `invitationVerifyEmailPromptPath`.
  - Four existing test files, which are not card-named:
    - `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/handoffVerificationMail-30157.test.tsx`
    - `ui/apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/verificationCallback-10893.test.tsx`
    - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/hooks/__tests__/useConsoleActionRuntime.apiActionDoor-27611.test.tsx`
    - `ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.apiActionDoor-27611.test.tsx`

### Should-fix
None.

### Notes
- N1: The rule is keyed on the code alone, so any `type: 'api'` action refused with it hands over to verification, and the mail's link returns to `/accept-invitation/<row id>`. Today only `accept_invitation` can produce that code from the inbox. If #34883 makes decline refusable too, its row id is still the invitation's, so the hand-over still lands on the right accept page. The report notes `reject_invitation`'s description will then owe the condition.
- N2: A deployment that sets `emailVerification.sendOnSignIn` will now see "send a link" after a sign-in refusal that did send one. Treating an unknown arrival as not sent is the stated default ("a page that cannot tell must not claim a mail went out"). The report notes that the opposite case on sign-up (`sendOnSignUp: false` with verification required) predates this PR.
- N3: The branch's commits carry no `Co-Authored-By` / `Claude-Session` trailer pair, and their subjects read `wip:`. The seat ruled at 16:36Z not to rewrite them. The queue squash takes the PR title, which is conventional.
- N4: This PR adds about 39 B to the eager `i18n-locale-en` chunk (61,857 / 62,000 on its own tree). Combined with #34925's 8 keys it would cross the current ceiling, so whichever lands second waits for #34927 (62,000 → 80,600), per the seat's ruling of 2026-11-17.

Landing: not governed, and all checks are green on this exact head. After the M1 amendment, area o3-H lands it. A later push owes a delta read.
